svg.title: Daily maximum: the curve against other forecasts
svg.desc: Per cent by which the curve's daily-maximum error is lower (positive) or higher (negative) than each other forecast's. Raw GFS: EDDM +30.3, KORD +6.0, CYYZ +22.2, ZGSZ +40.0, ZUCK +14.5, NZWN +56.5, EGLC +11.1, LFPG +20.1, KDSM +29.2, YSDU +5.5, KRNO +38.9, KSFO +27.4; AIFS: CYYZ +21.8, EDDM +6.9, EGLC +7.6, KDSM +13.5, KORD +21.7, KRNO +41.5, KSFO +19.6, LFPG +37.3, NZWN +59.8, YSDU +34.5, ZGSZ +24.8, ZUCK +8.8; ECMWF IFS: CYYZ +28.7, EDDM +12.5, EGLC +19.0, KDSM +13.0, KORD +20.9, KRNO +61.1, KSFO +23.3, LFPG +22.0, NZWN +50.0, YSDU +36.4, ZGSZ +44.6, ZUCK +21.9; NBM grid: CYYZ +14.0, KDSM +5.5, KORD +4.4, KRNO -1.5, KSFO +35.3; NBS: CYYZ +9.9, KDSM +0.4, KORD +2.5, KRNO +2.0, KSFO -1.1; MAV: KDSM +22.0, KORD +25.8, KRNO +15.7, KSFO +14.2.
svg.text: Daily maximum: the curve against other forecasts
Right of the line, the curve's error is lower. Left of the line, the other forecast's error is lower.
One dot per airport and forecast, with the 95% range. Each day's highest temperature.
filled dot: a formal test finds a real difference
diamond: raw GFS, no formal test was run on it
New airports (never used to choose settings)
Development airports (used to choose settings, so their figures flatter the curve a little)
per cent by which the curve's error is lower (right) or higher (left) than the other forecast's
Each forecast is compared with the curve only on the hours (or days) where both exist, so the curve's error differs a little between columns.
At the development airports AIFS and the NBM grid were read at GFS's grid point, not at the airport itself.
Descriptive, on years already used (2023-24 to 2025-26, depending on the source). Nothing is averaged across airports.
AIFS's daily maximum is the highest of its 6-hourly values and ECMWF IFS's the highest of its 3-hourly values, so each can miss the true peak.
